frontier.hypothesis: The disposition is a BLOCK question: game_2d_CheckLifeGaugeNoDisp, func_80052A88 and func_80052B7C are the same construct in the same contiguous authoring unit (0x80052A80-0x80052BDC) with the same single fill_delay rule, and func_80052B44 - already authorized - sits in the middle of the run.
frontier.mechanism: s8 F3/H21: these five are the complete set of tree functions whose jr $ra delay slot holds a cop2 op; they occupy consecutive addresses; four of them carry exactly one fill_delay regfix rule pulling the immediately preceding instruction (four of only six such rules tree-wide). Sessions 8-11's results are facts about GCC 2.7.2 (both forks), about ASPSX 2.34 and about reload's occupancy arithmetic - not about this function's C - so they apply verbatim.
frontier.next_probe: When a sibling reaches the queue top, do NOT re-derive sessions 1-11. Cite memory/grind/func_80052B00/evidence.md Sessions 8-11 plus s8/cop2_partition.txt, s8/slotcensus.txt, s9/fused8.psx.s, s10/dumps/ and s11/occ.sh; re-run only the cheap per-function confirmations (target tail shape, its single fill_delay rule, sandbox --disable all); take the disposition straight to the driver in one session.

frontier.hypothesis: engine/cheats.py does not strip a false clobber list on an asm whose template is real, so that spelling of the register-pin cheat is score-VISIBLE tree-wide and can masquerade as a floor drop.
frontier.mechanism: The stripper keys on empty-template asms and on register-asm pins; a clobber list attached to a legitimate non-empty template survives stripping while still steering reload1.c:3606 order_regs_for_reload(). Measured here as 2 vs 17 on the same body.
frontier.next_probe: Owner-side (grind sessions may not edit engine/): teach the cheat stripper to drop clobber-list entries naming hard GPRs that the template does not write, then re-run 'engine test' and re-score this function (expect 17) and any function whose ledger shows a large unexplained floor drop.
